Accept food rations being used as payment in kind

Allow FWB staff unescorted free movement inside the camp
Permit FWB nutritional assessments under escort

Extend food assistance to host-community families

goals.label: FWB staff and outsiders move freely and unescorted inside the camp
Food aid reaches the camp on an ongoing basis
Nutritional assessments and data collection on refugee needs are carried out
Aid food is diverted, skimmed or confiscated by camp authorities or militia
Commander's authority and image of strength are maintained
Control over the public narrative and outsider access to information
FWB staff and assistants are safe from threats and violence
Food functions as camp currency and payment
Guard and militia structures control food distribution
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Host town stability, economy and priority for local actors
Refugees face abuse or collective punishment, including food withholding
Refugees receive intended food fairly and equally
Refugees stay contained in the camp rather than reaching the capital
Commander retains the Senior Militia Leader's trust
FWB meets donor documentation and accountability requirements
FWB's operating methods and protocols are respected
Food is withheld from people labelled as suspected terrorists

redLines.label: Allow FWB and its chosen local assistants to manage disbursement directly
redLines.quote: If they hire local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Accept FWB will not feed guards and drop demand for food as guard pay
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

redLines.label: Prioritize local actors as distribution assistants
redLines.quote: If they hire local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Hire or prioritize local host-community actors such as MASHA as assistants and suppliers
redLines.quote: If they hire local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Manage food disbursement with FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants
redLines.quote: If they hire local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
